transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-29 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martin (Redwood AE), Carlos D'Souza (Redwood SE), Ivy Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (AstraGrid), Tom Alvarez (AstraGrid), Priya Nair (AstraGrid), Evan Soto (AstraGrid)

Summary (auto): Quick technical sync on AstraGrid marketplace connector, KMS compatibility (customer-managed KMS/HSM), and preflight items for on-prem packaged listing. Primary asks: confirm KMS key wrap support, network egress patterns for connector, Dedicated vs Hosted perf expectations, and marketplace packaging checklist.

Topics: KMS handshake and key wrapping, connector installation options (agent vs sidecar), V P C peering and firewall rules, Dedicated throughput bench, marketplace metadata and certs.

Action items (captured): see metadata action_items.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call — I'm Lena from Redwood and Carlos is here for the performance bits, Ivy for the packaging and marketplace checklist. Maya, could you quick intro on your side?
[00:22] Maya: Yep hi, Maya Chen, I run cloud partnerships at AstraGrid. We've got Tom on our platform team, Priya on security, Evan for ops. Goal today is to make sure the connector we want to list in their marketplace meets our KMS and air-gap requirements.
[00:40] Carlos: Cool, thanks. High level, Redwood supports three deployment patterns — hosted API, dedicated reserved GPU, and our private connector which you can run in your V P C or on prem. Today sounds like the private connector plus marketplace listing.
[01:05] Tom: Right. Our legal/compliance want the K M S keys to be customer-managed. We've seen vendors that only support cloud K M S and that's a blocker for us.
[01:20] Ivy: On the listing side, we typically need metadata, a minimal deployment manifest, and any certs for the connector packaging. We'll share a sample.
[01:35] Priya: On security, main questions: do you support bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys? Do you do envelope encryption/ key wrapping so secrets never leave our control? Also audit logs retention and tamper-evidence.
[01:55] Carlos: Short answer: yes, we support BYOK flows and we have a key-wrapping pattern — we call it the customer-key-wrap handshake in our docs — but I want to talk through network flows because that changes how the connector fetches keys. For HSM-backed keys we support both cloud K M S integrations and on-prem HSM via PKCS#11 bridge.
[02:20] Evan: Wait, PKCS11 — is that a connector we need to run inside our data center? Our infra team prefers a sidecar model rather than giving us another managed service instance.
[02:36] Carlos: You can run PKCS#11 bridge as a local daemon and our connector will talk to it over localhost. The connector itself can be deployed as a containerized service in your cluster — agent/sidecar mode — or as a standalone VM.
[02:55] Maya: For the marketplace listing we also need to declare supported deployment topologies. Is agent/sidecar fully supported and certified?
[03:12] Ivy: Yes. We have a certified agent pattern for on-prem. The main caveat is that some customers with strict egress rules need explicit firewall rules. We'll provide the egress IP ranges and ports.
[03:28] Priya: What ports? We can't just open wide ranges.
[03:34] Carlos: Primarily outbound TLS over 443 to our control plane for telemetry and config. For model inference traffic you can route directly to Dedicated endpoints in a cross-connect or through an egress NAT if you're on hosted. There is a fallback to our public endpoints if you choose that path. We'll send a minimal list.
[03:58] Tom: Can you clarify the telemetry data — is it application-level logs or token-level traces that could contain P I I?
[04:12] Lena: Important point — telemetry can be configured. By default we collect operational metrics and error traces (no user prompt text). For customers in Private mode we support disabling telemetry and pushing logs to your S3/KM using our log forwarder. But we need the logs for debugging during pilot; we propose a redacted-mode if needed.
[04:38] Priya: Redacted-mode sounds like an approach we'll accept as long as the raw payload is never stored in Redwood-managed cloud. We need to see the data flow diagram.
[04:50] Carlos: I'll attach a DFD in the follow-up. Also on KMS, there are two patterns: direct key referencing where connector requests KMS unwrap per session, or envelope encryption where the model-serving node only sees wrapped keys. Envelope is preferred for zero-trust.
[05:15] Evan: Envelope encryption — does that mean the keys for the KV cache are rotated per session? We have a very high write-read pattern on our prefix cache.
[05:30] Carlos: We rotate per deployment interval; not per token. Rotations can be frequent — we support daily rotations — but we don't rotate on every request for performance reasons. Our KV cache is encrypted at rest with the envelope-wrapped DEKs. That should meet your compliance.
[05:50] Maya: Ok, switching to marketplace packaging — Ivy, walk us through the docs we need to attach.
[05:58] Ivy: Sure. Minimum: product overview, deployment manifest (Helm chart or Terraform module), user guide, security whitepaper (incl. KMS/HSM integration steps), and a compatibility matrix. Also a small validation test script that the marketplace runner can execute to verify an install.
[06:20] Tom: For the validation test script — does Redwood provide a standard harness or do we write it?
[06:26] Ivy: We provide a test harness template. You'll need to fill in your endpoint specifics. For on-prem connectors, the harness checks connectivity, KMS unwrap operations with a test key, and a simple inference request against a small model to verify health.
[06:45] Priya: About audit logs retention and export — our compliance team wants logs shipped to our SIEM. Do you support pushing to customer S 3 or to syslog?
[06:57] Carlos: We support pushing to customer S3, and also have a syslog forwarder; for SIEM integrations we usually recommend S3+Lambda ingestion to avoid pushing raw logs into external collectors. We'll document the transforms.
[07:15] Evan: Network diagram — we're expecting the connector in our subnet, outbound to Redwood control plane, and calls to our internal K M S bridge. Any chance of an inbound connection from Redwood?
[07:28] Carlos: No inbound required for normal ops. During the listing cert run the marketplace runner may initiate a connectivity check — that runs from AWS/Azure infrastructure out to the connector's public endpoint if you expose one. For private installs we do a pull model.
[07:46] Maya: We also need to talk about packaging licensing. AstraGrid policy is to only list marketplace items that can run air-gapped. Are the installer artifacts self-contained?
[07:58] Ivy: Yes, we can produce a self-contained bundle (container images and a tarball) plus an offline validator. That is an extra step but we've done it for regulated customers.
[08:12] Priya: One more security question — HSM attestation and key provenance. If you support PKCS#11 bridge, can you attest the HSM firmware/slot IDs in logs so we can correlate?
[08:26] Carlos: We can surface HSM slot IDs in the audit logs and include attestation statements if the HSM supports it. That said, the exact attestation flow varies by vendor (nCipher vs AWS CloudHSM vs Gemalto) — we'll need details.
[08:42] Tom: Let's talk performance: if we run connector -> Dedicated (reserved GPU) pathway, what's realistic p95 latency for generation at 512 tokens?
[08:55] Carlos: In our Dedicated offering with optimal batching we typically see p95s in the 120–200ms range for 512 tokens on smaller models; large models obviously higher. But that's a broad range — we'll propose a throughput bench to replicate your token mix.
[09:15] Evan: Our approximate mix is 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64–512), 10% long. So batching matters.
[09:28] Carlos: Exactly. We'll ask for a workload sample to calibrate batching and the kernel selection. That feeds into the cost estimate as well.
[09:40] Lena: Quick note on cost and routing — you can route sensitive traffic to Dedicated and lower-priority queries to hosted fallbacks; that gives you an availability cushion.
[09:55] Maya: Marketplace certification also requires a support SLA and a test plan for patching. Ivy, do you handle the cert?
[10:03] Ivy: We'll help. There's a two-week certification window where the marketplace runner executes the validation script. We need the package and access details a week before that.
[10:14] Priya: Is there a pen-test requirement from Redwood? AstraGrid requires third-party pentest results for any listing.
[10:23] Lena: We do internal pen-tests and can share redacted reports. For customer listings we ask for customer-supplied pentest or to coordinate a joint assessment; we can add a clause to the listing notes.
[10:36] Tom: Ok, next — are there any known blockers integrating with our identity provider? We use SAML S S O with SCIM from Okta.
[10:48] Carlos: We support SAML S S O for the Console and SCIM for user provisioning. For the on-prem connector we can map caller identity to your IdP via SAML assertions; will need metadata.
[11:02] Evan: On the ops side, what's the upgrade path for a connector? We want to automate upgrades via our CI.
[11:12] Ivy: We publish semantic versions and a rolling upgrade strategy. For air-gapped installs, we'll provide an over-the-air bundle to your artifact repo and a standard rollback playbook.
[11:25] Maya: Sounds good. Let's capture next steps.
[11:30] Lena: Recap: Carlos will prepare perf/test plan and DFD; Ivy will share marketplace checklist and packaging examples; Lena will send listing metadata template and initial pricing guidance; Priya to send KMS policy questions; Evan to share network diagram. We'll follow up with a Dedicated bench slot for week of Jan 11.
[11:55] Priya: Quick clarifying Q — will Redwood require any long-term data retention on your side for logs?
[12:05] Carlos: No, for Private installs we respect customer retention. For hosted we have default 30-day logs but can adjust per contract.
[12:18] Tom: Great, thanks all.
[12:22] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll expect the docs in the next few days.
[12:27] Lena: Thank you — I'll send notes and the action items.

End of transcript.
